title: mitstack lifecycle webhook envelope
description: Versioned wire-shape contract for the JSON body mitstack's lifecycle engine POSTs to a block owner's registered webhook endpoint for each of the four alpha lifecycle verbs (subscribe/unsubscribe/upgrade/validate). Mirrors api/internal/lifecycle.Request byte-for-byte. Additive-friendly: additionalProperties is true at every level so a new optional Request field never breaks an existing operator or this contract test.

runId.description: The id the platform mints when it accepts a run and keeps on every send of it, so the block commits one request per run. Required on a run.

command.description: The one line of printable ASCII a run runs in a fresh container of the app's image. Required on a run.

process.description: The process of the part a run runs in, such as web. A run that names none runs in the block's entry, the process that serves the app's address.

unit.description: The name of the spec.continuity entry a snapshot or a restore is for. Required on both.

replacing.description: True on every request sent during a replacement, which tells the block to send no install retry.

leaseId.description: The id a lease keeps on every attempt, so the provider can tell a retry from a new lease. A lease carries it to mint a credential and leaves it out to only retire some.

want.description: What the caller asks of a lease, an object the platform forwards and never reads and the provider reads for the signals or links it should mint for.

retire.description: The provider's handles of the credentials a lease asks it to delete, which it answered on earlier leases and which have lapsed.

caller.description: The subscription that asked for a lease and the blocks the platform records as bound to it, which bound what the provider may mint. Required on a lease that mints.

capabilitySlug.description: The slug of the capability a verify-connection asks its operator to check a credential for. Required on a verify-connection, which carries no subscription, block or app.

enteredCredential.description: The fields of the credential a person entered to connect their org, keyed by the capability's token field names, which a verify-connection hands the operator to check. Its values are secret. Required on a verify-connection.

issueAppId.description: The app an issue asks the capability to issue a credential for. Required on an issue.

resource.description: The name of the one resource the block's manifest declares that a validate observes. Omitted, the verb runs on every declared resource, in creation order and in reverse for a teardown. A block refuses a name on any verb but validate.

resourceIdentity.description: The identity the ensure of the resource named under resource stored, the values that address it where it lives, keyed by name. Present only with a non-empty resource.

resourceUnsubscribing.description: True when the validate naming one resource under resource probes it during a teardown, so the resource's observer answers as it does during an unsubscribe. Omitted, the probe is not a teardown's.

resourceType.description: The exact type the resource named under resource was created as, one of the types its manifest entry lists. Present only with a non-empty resource.

recordedResources.description: What the engine recorded for each resource the block's manifest declares, keyed by the resource's name: the type it was created as and the identity that addresses it.

type.description: The exact type the resource was created as.

identity.description: The values that address the resource where it lives, keyed by name.

state.description: Set only when the engine has already recorded the resource absent, so an unsubscribe neither deletes nor observes it.

settlesAt.description: The time of the state-changing verb a validate settles. An observe reads only what was made after it. Omitted, the request settles itself, at its createdAt.

neverActive.description: True only when the engine has proved the subscription holds no user data yet: it never reached active, and it was not created from a data handover such as a stack switch's restored snapshot. A block may then replace a stateful resource. False or omitted, every stateful resource stays guarded.

absences.description: The platform's attestation, keyed by the requirement's reference, that its own observer read the bound provider's resource absent. Each entry names the observer, the resource and the time it read absent, and provesAbsence takes the meaning of a node report's reportSignature.provesAbsence. A block honours an entry only when provesAbsence is true and the three are named. Omitted, nothing is attested.

requirementTypes.description: The exact type of the resource that met each of the block's requirements, keyed by the requirement's reference.

operation.description: The lifecycle verb being dispatched, issue, which asks a capability for one app's credential, logs, which asks a block for the subscription's recent lines on /logs, verify-connection, which asks a capability's operator whether the credential an org entered works, lease, which asks a block for a short-lived credential of a resource it provides or to retire the ones it minted, run, which asks a block to run a builder's one-off command in a fresh container of the app, snapshot, which asks a block to snapshot one declared state and publish its handover once a scratch restore of it passes, or restore, which asks it to put that state back from the handover.

appId.description: The consuming app that owns the subscription (m-7). Additive: operators that predate app-ownership simply ignore it.

params.description: Manifest-declared, non-secret param values, resolved server-side.

instances.description: Resolved tool instances keyed by capability, scoped to the block's requires[] (T-062).

secrets.description: Plaintext secrets resolved server-side, keyed by capability then by secret name. Redacted before any audit log.

obo.description: On-behalf-of token minted by the engine (T-095), signed with the block's lifecycle secret, encoding org/app/subscription identity.

secretInputs.description: Resolved plaintext for the block's secret params, the inputs a type it creates marks secret, keyed by param name.

ownSecrets.description: The own secrets this subscription's block returned on earlier calls, keyed by the names the block chose. No request of another subscription carries them. Omitted while the subscription keeps none.

bindings.description: Outputs from the first active provider subscription of a required capability, keyed by capability (T-153).

bindingsAll.description: Outputs from EVERY active provider of a required capability, keyed by capability (fan-in, m-55).

cloudIdentity.description: Federated cloud-account identity for an org with a CONNECTED cloud_connection (m-24 / T-193). Nil/omitted when no connected connection exists.

roleArn.description: Provider-specific federated identity: an IAM role ARN (aws), the WIF pool/provider resource (gcp), or a "<tenantId>/<clientId>" composite (azure).

accountRef.description: Additional account reference (T-464) — e.g. the gcp impersonation service-account email.

priorOutputs.description: The subscription's own previously-recorded outputs, handed back to the operator that produced them (MIT-1950). Present only on the teardown direction — unsubscribe, and a validate call issued as part of a teardown's absence probe — never on a validate/subscribe/upgrade call issued as part of ordinary provisioning or polling. Account-identifying values are deliberately not here: those travel via secrets, exactly like any other teardown call.

createdAt.description: RFC 3339 timestamp set by the engine per delivery attempt; anchors OBO expiry checks and, with nonce, bounds replay skew (T-357).

nonce.description: Fresh random value regenerated for every delivery attempt, covered by the Ed25519 signature, so a captured signed request cannot be replayed (T-357).
